column1: Word choice must stay a human judgment.
column2: people must choose the words of the lexicon. machines must not choose the words of the lexicon.

column1: …the critical safety property is exactly the kind of check humans miss and machines don't.
column2: people cannot find every collision. machines can find every collision.

column1: A hand-edited seed/seed.json is the single source of truth.
column2: people edit the file "seed.json". the file "seed.json" is the source of the truth.

column1: Every curation commit shows its effect in the diffs.
column2: every commit shows the effect of the commit in the diffs

column1: Both generated files are committed; they are build outputs and are never hand-edited.
column2: the repository has the generated files. people do not edit the generated files.

column1: Curation stays human and cheap: one JSON entry per word; the machine owns inflection and safety.
column2: people choose the words. every word has one entry. the machine writes the inflections and finds the collisions.

column1: Reference data is used only for checking - never for choosing words.
column2: the linter checks the words with the data. the data does not choose the words.
